name: Sofia Kourtesis
label: Ninja Tune
lede: Sofia Kourtesis left Lima for Germany at 17 and, by her own account, rapped badly in Hamburg. Years later she made Madres while her mother was being treated for cancer, and it landed on Pitchfork's 2023 year-end list.

eras.title: Lima to Hamburg to Berlin
eras.text: Raised in Lima under the Fujimori years, she was on a plane to Germany at 17. Hamburg, film school in Berlin and a short, self-confessed bad run as a rapper came before any house records.

q: I was a very bad rapper.
years.src: Wikipedia: Sofia Kourtesis · DJ Mag: Pursuit of happiness · NME: Madres interview · The Guardian: My mother's neurosurgeon
years.h: Born in Magdalena, Lima, Kourtesis is on a plane to Germany at 17
years.p: She grew up in Lima's Magdalena district under the Fujimori years. She left Peru as a teenager, first for Hamburg and then Berlin, where she studied film.
years.xp:
DJ Mag reports she grew up under Alberto Fujimori's regime with activist parents who felt threatened, and that she was bullied and sent through conversion therapy as a teenager after being caught kissing a girl at school. NME reports she was expelled for it.

In her early 20s in Hamburg she rapped in a German-language hip-hop group. "I was a very bad rapper," she told DJ Mag. She later worked as a programmer at Berlin's Funkhaus, the former East German radio complex.

eras.title: Barnhus and the EP run
eras.text: Her first releases trickled out of Berlin. Then a Swedish label, Studio Barnhus, turned a DJ and club programmer into a producer people sought out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sofia Kourtesis · DJ Mag: Pursuit of happiness
years.h: Her first EP, This Is It, comes out on Duchess Box
years.p: DJ Mag lists an early collaboration with Gold Panda, "Las Magnolias", from the same year.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates This Is It to 28 November 2014 on Duchess Box. DJ Mag names her 2014 collaboration with Gold Panda, "Las Magnolias", as one of her early releases.

years.src: DJ Mag: Pursuit of happiness · The Guardian: My mother's neurosurgeon · RA: Madres review
years.h: "WinWin San" gets her onto Studio Barnhus
years.p: DJ Mag picked the track out as the standout of a Barnhus compilation. It opens the Swedish label's run of Kourtesis releases.
years.xp: The Guardian and DJ Mag both point to 2018 and "WinWin San" as the start of her Barnhus period. RA later described her as primarily associated with the Swedish label before Ninja Tune.

years.h: Sofia Kourtesis, her first full EP for Barnhus
years.p: Studio Barnhus released it on 28 February 2019.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sofia Kourtesis · DJ Mag: Pursuit of happiness
years.h: Valentine's Day, and Sarita Colonia is out
years.p: The second Barnhus EP arrived just before lockdown.
years.xp: DJ Mag says a pandemic-era realization changed how she worked: she stopped asking whether she was "Tresor enough" or "Latin enough" and committed to being honest.

eras.title: Grief, Manu Chao and a breakout year
eras.text: Grief turned her into a singer, Ninja Tune's Technicolour imprint took her in, and a Manu Chao vocal became the hopeful centerpiece of a breakout year.

years.src: NME: La Perla interview · Wikipedia: Sofia Kourtesis · DJ Mag: Pursuit of happiness
years.h: Fresia Magdalena is named for her mother and her neighborhood
years.p: Her first release with her own voice on it came out on Ninja Tune's Technicolour imprint. "La Perla" is written for her father.
years.xp: NME reports the title points to her mother, Fresia, and Magdalena del Mar, where she grew up. It was her first record with her own voice on it. "La Perla" is dedicated to her father's leukemia, per NME, and DJ Mag says he died of it.

years.cap: Kourtesis live at L'Aeronef, Lille, March 18, 2022
years.h: Manu Chao sings on "Estación Esperanza" over a protest tape
years.p: The Ninja Tune single carries Manu Chao's vocal and field recordings of Peruvian protesters against homophobic violence.
years.xp:
Mixmag carried her statement: "I first wrote this song after listening to Manu Chao. To me Manu Chao has always represented hope." She described the track as about hope for her mother's recovery and for social change.

It later became the lead-in to her debut album.

years.h: BBC Radio 1 hands her the Essential Mix
years.p: It aired on 9 April 2022, per MixesDB's listing.

years.cap: Kourtesis at the Sonic stage, Glastonbury, June 2022
years.src: MixesDB: Boiler Room Stockholm · Wikipedia: Sofia Kourtesis · NME: Madres interview
years.p: MixesDB lists the Boiler Room set on 25 May 2022. Wikipedia's photo caption puts her at Glastonbury the same year.
years.xp: NME's profile says she supported Bicep and Caribou on tour and learned from Caribou's Dan Snaith.

eras.title: Madres
eras.text: The debut album followed a stretch of flights between Lima and Berlin while her mother fought cancer. Pitchfork put it at No. 24 for 2023.

years.cap: Kourtesis on stage at Pitchfork Music Festival, Chicago
years.src: The Guardian: My mother's neurosurgeon · NME: Madres interview · Wikipedia: Madres (album)
years.h: Her mother's neurosurgeon gets a track, and a night at Berghain
years.p: Peter Vajkoczy, the Berlin neurosurgeon who operated on her mother's cancer, is the subject of "Vajkoczy", co-written with Johnetta Bryant.
years.xp:
The Guardian reports Kourtesis contacted Vajkoczy after her mother was diagnosed with metastatic lung cancer, and that she later took him to Berghain. NME says she reached him over Instagram and that her mother now lives in Berlin.

Her father, a pro bono lawyer during the Fujimori dictatorship, had died before she made the record, per The Guardian.

years.src: Wikipedia: Madres (album) · The Guardian: My mother's neurosurgeon · NME: Madres interview
years.h: Madres: Best New Music, then No. 24 for the year
years.p: Pitchfork gave the debut album 8.5 and Best New Music. Metacritic lists 86/100.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists production from Kourtesis, David Krasemann and Thomas Stephens, and guests Manu Chao and Johnetta Bryant. The Guardian notes the Ballumbrosio family of Afro-Peruvian percussion appear on "El Carmen".

NME reports her 2023 motto as "Less perfection, more corazón." It reached No. 2 on the UK Dance Albums chart, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Volver
eras.text: Back on Ninja Tune with a short EP built around community and family, and her first collaboration with Daphni.

years.cap: Kourtesis at a festival set, c. 2025
years.src: Ninja Tune: Volver · Wikipedia: Sofia Kourtesis
years.p: The six-track EP includes "Unidos" with Daphni (Dan Snaith of Caribou) and "Ballumbrosio" with Miguel Ballumbrosio.
years.xp: Ninja Tune describes the EP as a tribute to the LGBT+ community and trans women. Kourtesis calls Snaith "a hero" and says she made it while touring, doing community work, caring for her mother and starting medical studies.
